items.summary: Bulls forward Caleb Wilson spoke to the media on Friday for the first time since he fractured his right hand and expressed optimism that he’ll return to action sooner rather than later, according to Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic (Twitter video link). When asked about the specific incident that broke his hand, this year’s No. 4 overall pick said he immediately knew something was wrong. “I looked down at my hand and it was bent the wrong way,” Wilson said. “So I just, I knew something was up. And I heard it.” Wilson, who suffered the injury on November 11 and underwent surgery the following day, is expected to miss another three-to-five weeks. He said Friday that he didn’t anticipate missing most of the season. “It’s difficult, but it’s not long term. I’ll play again in a couple weeks, not really worried about it,” said Wilson, who clarified that he didn’t have a set timetable for his…

items.title: Moritz Wagner’s first-ever chance to face his brother Franz is nothing short of ‘awkward’
items.summary: Nets wagnerBrooklyn’s Moritz Wagner has been in the NBA for nine years and alive for 20 more, and he had never, ever played against his brother, Franz, in a game that counted. That is, until Friday night. The Wagner siblings faced off when the Nets hosted Franz’s Orlando Magic, and they squared off against each other for the first time. “It’s awkward, I’m not gonna lie. I don’t really know how to compartmentalize it, really deal with it, and try to focus on the game plan and see what happens emotionally,” Moritz said beforehand. “It’s a dilemma because you want him to do well. At the same time, you game plan for him, you prepare to limit him. So, it’s an awkward feeling. I’ve never been in this position. items.title: Jazz’s Jusuf Nurkic (Toe) Out At Least One More Week
items.summary: Veteran center Jusuf Nurkic will be sidelined at least one more week due to the toe injury on his right foot, the Jazz announced in a press release. According to the team, Nurkic is making progress in his recovery and has been participating in on-court work. The 32-year-old big man will be reevaluated again in a week. Nurkic suffered a partial plantar plate tear of the second toe in his right foot during Utah’s preseason opener on October 4. He has been sidelined for the past six-plus weeks and will miss at least one more. Nurkic was limited to 41 appearances in 2025/26, his first season in Utah, but he made 36 starts and averaged 10.9 points, 10.4 rebounds and 4.8 assists in 26.4 minutes per night while shooting 50.3% from the field. The team has yet to make any sort of formal announcement regarding Prince’s procedure, but as beat reporters Hunter Patterson of The Athletic and Omari Sankofa II of The Detroit Free Press note (via Twitter), the veteran’s designation on Detroit’s injury report has been updated from “right knee soreness” to “right knee surgery.” Presumably, the Pistons will provide an update at some point soon on Prince’s surgery and his potential return timeline, but it sounds like he won’t be available for the foreseeable future.
